notes:
POC account for real-time agent assist (streaming suggestions). Primary ask: sub-150ms per-suggestion latency end-to-end with guardrails. Heavy emphasis on reliability under agent spikes (aiming for 3-5k concurrent live agents; burst to 10k). Wants streaming token-level suggestions so UI can highlight next-sentence and canned responses as agent types.

Key constraints / asks: short bullets, CRM style -
- Low-latency SLOs: 50-150ms target for 1-2 token suggestion completions; 200ms acceptable for longer suggestions.
- Guardrails: PII/PCI redaction (client redacts driver-license, cc numbers), deterministic response filters, allow-list for task-specific commands. Need audit logs for every suggestion and tool call.
- Tool-calling: must be able to execute CRM update calls and dialer actions from model output (function-calling with strict parameter schema). Telephony routing will be via Twilio; need webhook auth details.
- Reliability: prefer Dedicated or Private with VPC so they can meet compliance. Want autoscaling profile that prioritizes latency over cost during business hours.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-level; will accept higher cost for dedicated latency guarantees but need Optimize recommendations to reduce per-token spend (quantization + batching rules).

Quote from CTO on 2025-02-17 call: "We can live with slightly higher unit cost if agent AHT drops 10% and NPS goes up — latency and reliability are everything."

POC plan: run 3-week dedicated POC. Week 1: integration and baseline latency. Week 2: synthetic spike tests across 0.5k->5k concurrent agents. Week 3: live shadowing with 50 agents and progressive rollouts. Deliverables: perf report, cost model, security attestation.

Open items: kerberos for on-prem infra, KMS key exchange flow, telemetry retention retention window (currently default 30d, they need 13 months), SLA language for failover across regions.

Stubs/refs: drive pricing + security FAQ, fireflies recs (see ff_20250310_lattice-poc). Jira ticket CCSUP-3421 created for telephony auth failure seen during spike test.
